description: Browsable, non-prescriptive intervention directions across distinct modalities and life contexts. This pass expands choices and what progress may look like; formal baselines, numeric targets, deadlines, efficacy rankings and patient-specific selection are deferred until clinical review. All clinical interventions require appropriate qualifications, consent, safety assessment and contextual formulation.

interventions.title: Collaborative anxiety formulation
interventions.try: In session, map the feared meaning, context, attention, responses and consequences of a real situation. Examine realistic danger and access needs before selecting a change.
interventions.measure: Review whether the explanation fits the person's experience and identifies workable choices.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided approach experiment
interventions.try: Assess actual risks and needed accommodations, negotiate a voluntary manageable experiment, coach during it and debrief predictions against what occurred.
interventions.measure: Track chosen participation and learning; do not treat anxiety reduction as the sole outcome.
interventions.scope: Clinician screens medical/safety issues; never remove necessary accommodations.

interventions.title: Clinical accommodation experiment
interventions.try: Jointly analyze which demands create barriers and which responses reflect fear. In session compare feasible access changes, enlist relevant partners with consent, and review impacts.
interventions.measure: Compare participation, effort and overload in equivalent situations with and without the support.

interventions.title: Behavioral activation with therapist formulation
interventions.try: Map mood, fatigue, overload, rewards and opportunity restrictions. Use a session to choose and troubleshoot accessible, meaningful activity experiments with the person.
interventions.measure: Compare personally meaningful engagement and feasibility over repeated opportunities.

interventions.title: Guided work on self-critical beliefs
interventions.try: Help the person examine a self-critical conclusion, evidence, life context and possible alternatives. Rehearse a personally credible response in session.
interventions.measure: Use individualized self-criticism ratings alongside functioning and personally valued action.

interventions.title: Relapse signature and coordinated response plan
interventions.try: Map the person's pattern of sleep, activation, mood and functioning across episodes; distinguish baseline variation and medication effects. Coordinate a response plan with the treating team.
interventions.measure: Track individualized early warning changes, plan use and functional stability.
interventions.scope: Requires appropriate coordination with prescribing care; never substitute for urgent mania, psychosis or safety assessment.

interventions.title: Therapist-facilitated family support planning
interventions.try: With consent, help the person and supporters define what changes should prompt contact, which help is welcome and who makes which decisions. Rehearse the plan together.
interventions.measure: Monitor whether helpful actions are available when needed while autonomy is respected.

interventions.title: Therapist-led worry differentiation
interventions.try: In session distinguish solvable problems, uncertain outcomes and unavoidable demands. Guide appropriate problem-solving and values-based uncertainty work rather than using one technique for everything.
interventions.measure: Track time lost to repetitive worry, problem actions completed and tolerable uncertainty.

interventions.title: Uncertainty tolerance rehearsal
interventions.try: Together choose a low-risk decision, assess the need for more information, guide one decision without repeated guarantees and process what the person learned.
interventions.measure: Compare decision participation and checking/reassurance burden across comparable choices.

interventions.title: Panic-cycle case formulation
interventions.try: In session, use an actual event to map sensation, interpretation, alarm, response and possible recurrence. Check medical and contextual explanations and identify a collaborative treatment focus.
interventions.measure: Ask how accurately the cycle captures episodes and whether the person can identify useful next steps.
interventions.scope: New, severe or changed symptoms need medically appropriate evaluation.

interventions.title: Clinician-supervised panic experiment
interventions.try: When medically appropriate, a qualified therapist formulates feared predictions, obtains consent, structures an exposure/response experiment and debriefs outcomes together.
interventions.measure: Track prediction learning and restored chosen participation, not induced symptoms for their own sake.
interventions.scope: Interoceptive exposure requires indicated medical screening and qualified supervision.

interventions.title: Therapist-led interpersonal rehearsal
interventions.try: Explore the real communication demand, then model and rehearse a chosen interaction in session. Give collaborative feedback and support culturally and neurodevelopmentally appropriate styles.
interventions.measure: Evaluate usable self-advocacy, choice and communication access instead of eye contact or conformity.

interventions.title: Social evaluation hypothesis test
interventions.try: In session, help the person formulate one fear of being judged; check actual discrimination or relationship danger. Design a consented experiment or role-play and compare prediction and observed outcomes.
interventions.measure: Measure personally meaningful engagement and accuracy of predictions in context.

interventions.title: Collaborative graded exposure treatment
interventions.try: A qualified therapist evaluates safety, consent and functional aims, develops a flexible hierarchy, guides graded approach and processes learning.
interventions.measure: Track voluntary participation and feared outcome learning alongside accommodations.
interventions.scope: No unsafe exposures or pressure to override consent/medical advice.

interventions.title: Specialist ERP formulation and practice
interventions.try: An OCD-qualified clinician differentiates obsessions, rituals, reassurance and necessary safety actions; agrees on exposure/response prevention targets, coaches practice and revisits effects.
interventions.measure: Monitor time or interference from compulsions and return to chosen life activities.
interventions.scope: Do not confuse legitimate safety, medical care, disability supports or eating care with rituals.

interventions.title: Family accommodation consultation
interventions.try: With consent, identify which reassurance patterns may unintentionally reinforce compulsions and which are genuine support needs. Co-design nonpunitive changes and rehearse responses with supporters.
interventions.measure: Track supporter confidence and whether useful assistance remains accessible.

interventions.title: Body-image meaning and checking formulation
interventions.try: In session, collaboratively explore appearance beliefs, mirror/photo checking, shame, social pressures and avoidance. Use a structured case formulation to select a treatment approach without debating actual appearance.
interventions.measure: Track distress and interference plus chosen social/work participation.

interventions.title: Trauma-informed stabilization and shared formulation
interventions.try: Assess readiness, current safety, dissociation, supports and goals. Collaboratively link triggers and responses while avoiding unnecessary trauma detail, and select an appropriate phase of care.
interventions.measure: Monitor perceived safety, choice, coping effectiveness and functional participation.
interventions.scope: Trauma-processing treatments require suitable qualification and informed consent.

interventions.title: Specialist trauma-focused therapy
interventions.try: A qualified therapist uses an evidence-based trauma-focused method with individualized pacing, consent, response monitoring and active reassessment of stability and goals.
interventions.measure: Use appropriate symptom and function measures plus the person's assessment of safety and benefit.
interventions.scope: Do not treat this prompt as a protocol for unsupervised trauma exposure.

interventions.title: Collaborative transition-focused problem solving
interventions.try: Structure sessions around what changed, controllable and uncontrollable demands, losses, supports and person-defined priorities. Rehearse communication and one feasible adjustment strategy.
interventions.measure: Track goal progress, role participation and felt agency during the transition.

interventions.title: Grief-focused therapeutic meaning work
interventions.try: In session, with sensitivity to culture and relationship, help the person explore loss-related distress, changing roles, ongoing bonds and wishes for connection without prescribing a timetable.
interventions.measure: Review impairment, meaningful connection and personally valued adaptation rather than grief 'completion'.

interventions.title: Dissociation-focused grounding and continuity planning
interventions.try: A trained therapist assesses episodes and safety, identifies individualized early signs, practices consensual grounding or orientation methods in session and documents what helps or worsens functioning.
interventions.measure: Record orientation, participation, aftereffects and support needs across contexts.
interventions.scope: Avoid suggestive memory-recovery techniques or assuming one explanatory model.

interventions.title: Non-leading functional dissociation assessment
interventions.try: Use careful phenomenological questions and functional observation to distinguish experiences, triggers, memory problems and possible medical causes; coordinate indicated assessment.
interventions.measure: Track time lost, continuity of daily roles and changes reported in a neutral language.

interventions.title: Therapist-delivered interpersonal chain analysis
interventions.try: In session, with a collaborative and nonjudgmental approach, review a difficult interpersonal event, vulnerabilities, cue, actions, consequences and alternatives, without assuming intent or blame.
interventions.measure: Monitor relationship functioning, repair choices and ability to apply an agreed skill.

interventions.title: Structured emotion-regulation skills therapy
interventions.try: In session teach, model and rehearse an indicated skill; help the person adapt it for sensory or access needs, troubleshoot obstacles and review use without punitive compliance targets.
interventions.measure: Measure function after difficult emotions, skill usefulness and chosen safety goals.

interventions.title: Longitudinal interpersonal pattern formulation
interventions.try: The therapist and person explore repeated relationship themes across settings and time, including contextual harms, strengths and alternative explanations. Revise the formulation collaboratively.
interventions.measure: Review valued relationships, self-understanding and functioning rather than an assumed personality label.

interventions.title: Collaborative coping and relapse-support planning
interventions.try: Assess immediate risks and strengths, discuss distressing experiences without confrontation, coordinate with psychiatric care and negotiate usable coping and help-seeking responses.
interventions.measure: Track distress, role functioning, adherence to chosen supports and ability to obtain timely care.
interventions.scope: Medication and acute risk decisions belong to qualified medical teams.

interventions.title: CBT-informed work with distressing experiences
interventions.try: A trained clinician collaboratively examines meaning, threat and coping around unusual experiences without forcing agreement about their cause. Test safer alternatives only when appropriate.
interventions.measure: Monitor distress, agency, sleep and daily participation; symptoms alone do not measure benefit.

interventions.title: Therapist-led executive-function design
interventions.try: Observe task demands and access barriers, co-design external structure, practice a realistic task sequence in session and iteratively adjust cues with the person's feedback.
interventions.measure: Measure initiation latency, completion with supports and cognitive effort.

interventions.title: In-session task initiation coaching
interventions.try: In session, rehearse identifying the smallest functional step, arranging materials, planning a restart cue and handling interruptions during an actual selected task.
interventions.measure: Track supported starting and restarting across real opportunities.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided sensory and demand assessment
interventions.try: In session, map sensory demands, unpredictability and communication access across contexts. Trial environmental changes collaboratively rather than imposing habituation or masking.
interventions.measure: Compare participation, aftereffects, recovery cost and the person's choice.

interventions.title: Affirming communication-access intervention
interventions.try: With the person, adjust communication methods and practice boundaries or support requests in session; include partners only with consent and avoid enforcing normative social behavior.
interventions.measure: Measure whether authentic communication, refusals and preferences are understood and respected.

interventions.title: Supported decision-making assessment and coaching
interventions.try: Assess which accessible information, response methods and trusted supports make choices possible. Rehearse presenting real options, checking understanding and respecting refusal.
interventions.measure: Track opportunities offered, preferences expressed and choices honored.
interventions.scope: Do not infer global capacity from speech or one response.

interventions.title: Clinician-guided adaptive support experiment
interventions.try: Observe a person-chosen daily task with consent, identify environmental or communication barriers, model aids/supports and review participation without equating assistance with failure.
interventions.measure: Compare role participation and needed support; monitor dignity and effort.

interventions.title: Caregiver-child functional consultation
interventions.try: Assess safety and context, collect descriptive before/behavior/after observations, and collaboratively coach caregivers in co-regulation, predictable routines and repair.
interventions.measure: Track frequency with context, child safety, caregiver consistency and improved function.
interventions.scope: Avoid coercion or interpreting all distress as willful misconduct.

interventions.title: In-session caregiver skill rehearsal
interventions.try: In session, model one specific validation, limit-setting or co-regulation response; rehearse it with the caregiver and help plan a feasible real-world context for trying it.
interventions.measure: Monitor caregiver response quality, child safety and opportunities for child communication.

interventions.title: Clinician-guided escalation chain and interruption
interventions.try: Review a recent escalation from context to body signs, threat meaning, available choices and consequences. Rehearse a preferred pause, boundary or recovery response in session.
interventions.measure: Track time to notice early cues, harm reduction and successful safe reconnection.

interventions.title: Motivational interviewing for ambivalence
interventions.try: The trained therapist elicits the person's values and concerns with a nonjudgmental stance, clarifies ambivalence and collaborates on harm-reduction or treatment goals without coercion.
interventions.measure: Record self-chosen goals, engagement and functional change.
interventions.scope: Withdrawal and overdose risks require appropriate medical assessment.

interventions.title: Relapse/return-to-use safety planning
interventions.try: Explore triggers, access, relationships and practical barriers; coordinate medications or specialty care as indicated, and rehearse a nonpunitive re-entry plan after a setback.
interventions.measure: Monitor risk reduction, timely access to services and personally meaningful functioning.
interventions.scope: Do not replace medically managed withdrawal or prescribing care.

interventions.title: Eating-disorder multidisciplinary coordination
interventions.try: An appropriately trained clinician helps coordinate medical/nutritional monitoring, family or support involvement with consent, and individualized psychological care within scope.
interventions.measure: Review medical status with the team and patient-centered participation; avoid relying on body size alone.
interventions.scope: Medical instability and refeeding decisions require qualified specialist oversight.

interventions.title: Specialist eating-disorder cognitive work
interventions.try: Within coordinated care, assess rules, fear, self-evaluation, access needs and maintaining context. Use a collaboratively selected treatment model without prescribing restriction or numeric intake goals here.
interventions.measure: Review functioning, psychological flexibility and medically reviewed progress.
interventions.scope: Not a self-help exposure or refeeding protocol.

interventions.title: Specialist binge/purge pattern formulation
interventions.try: With qualified care, map contextual triggers, cycles, compensatory behavior and physical risk. Select coordinated evidence-based treatment components and ensure medical review.
interventions.measure: Monitor frequency and harm, functioning, and agreed clinical indicators without shaming.
interventions.scope: Electrolyte and other medical risks require appropriate assessment.

interventions.title: Therapist-supported eating-rule flexibility
interventions.try: Explore rigid rules and shame in a consented, specialist setting; co-design safer behavior-change work coordinated with nutritional/medical care.
interventions.measure: Monitor reduced impairment and sustainable participation, with medical outcomes interpreted by the team.

interventions.title: Multidisciplinary feeding access formulation
interventions.try: Distinguish sensory, fear, appetite, swallowing, nutritional and environmental contributors with appropriate specialist assessment; adapt context and meal access with consent.
interventions.measure: Review nutritional/medical stability, tolerable participation and accommodation effectiveness.
interventions.scope: Do not prescribe unmonitored food exposures or assume no medical risk.

interventions.title: Clinician-led graded food participation
interventions.try: Qualified clinicians, with appropriate medical/nutritional clearance, collaboratively structure noncoercive, paced food-participation work and adjust to sensory/communication needs.
interventions.measure: Track choice, functional eating participation and medical safety as assessed by the team.
interventions.scope: No pressure, forced intake or substitution for indicated medical evaluation.

interventions.title: CBT-I sleep-pattern formulation
interventions.try: A qualified clinician reviews a structured sleep diary, daytime functioning, medications and relevant medical causes; identifies an appropriate treatment component and checks safety.
interventions.measure: Measure sleep patterns alongside daytime participation and unwanted effects.
interventions.scope: Sleep restriction is not a generic self-help exercise; screen for bipolar, seizure and other relevant risks.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided sleep environment review
interventions.try: Assess noise, light, pain, caregiving demands, neurodivergent needs and routines with the person; prioritize realistic modifications and review impact.
interventions.measure: Compare sleep continuity and daytime fatigue across feasible changes.

interventions.title: Integrated symptom-and-care formulation
interventions.try: Validate the reported symptoms and suffering, review indicated medical care, stress and attention patterns without prematurely psychologizing, and coordinate a shared care plan.
interventions.measure: Measure functional burden, care access and quality of life as well as symptom distress.
interventions.scope: Do not use symptom response to rule out disease or delay appropriate investigation.

interventions.title: Collaborative medical communication session
interventions.try: Help the person prepare questions and a coherent account of symptoms and functional impact; with consent coordinate expectations among treating clinicians.
interventions.measure: Track whether medically indicated follow-up occurred and whether the person felt heard and could function.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided pacing and participation design
interventions.try: In session, differentiate flare patterns, medical guidance, accessible effort and valued activities. Collaboratively build flexible pacing based on sustainable participation instead of mandatory pushing.
interventions.measure: Track chosen activities, recovery time, flare impact and burden of the plan.

interventions.title: Pain-related threat and coping formulation
interventions.try: In session examine perceived threat, lived constraints, uncertainty, avoidance and supports without dismissing pain as psychological. Integrate with appropriate medical treatment.
interventions.measure: Measure function, agency, pain interference and whether the person's concerns receive appropriate care.

interventions.title: Cognitive-access and environment consultation
interventions.try: In a clinician-led review, with the person and appropriate supports, evaluate memory, comprehension, wayfinding and functional safety; trial simpler cues and adaptations to daily routines.
interventions.measure: Track successful chosen tasks with supports and caregiver burden rather than unaided performance alone.

interventions.title: Supported communication and care planning
interventions.try: In a clinician-led conversation, facilitate accessible discussion of preferences, goals, roles and future supports, accounting for decision-specific ability, communication needs and consent.
interventions.measure: Review whether choices are expressed and honored, participation preserved and supports realistically available.

interventions.title: Regulation skills fitted to the person's nervous system
interventions.try: In session, the therapist explores what overload feels like and rehearses several chosen settling or orientation approaches, adjusting for sensory needs and past adverse reactions.
interventions.measure: Notice which approaches improve access, steadiness, agency and participation rather than demanding immediate calm.

interventions.title: Work on reassurance and helpful support
interventions.try: The therapist and person map when requests for help provide needed access versus when repetitive reassurance briefly reduces fear. They rehearse responses that preserve safety, connection and choice.
interventions.measure: Review whether supportive relationships remain available and whether worry interferes less with personally meaningful decisions.

interventions.title: Therapist-supported barrier removal
interventions.try: In session, examine how illness, money, caregiving, pain, executive demands, social isolation or access barriers constrain action. Co-develop practical supports alongside psychological treatment.
interventions.measure: Notice feasible re-entry to personally valued roles and reduction of unnecessary effort or obstacles.

interventions.title: Interpersonal therapy focus on role and connection
interventions.try: A qualified therapist helps the person explore grief, role transitions, conflict and relational patterns when indicated, with collaborative communication work that respects actual safety and context.
interventions.measure: Review relational satisfaction, support access, meaningful connection and depressive interference.

interventions.title: Collaborative episode interpretation and self-management
interventions.try: In session, a clinician and person review early episode signals, what those signals have and have not predicted, relevant medications and context, and how to respond without overpathologizing everyday changes.
interventions.measure: Notice earlier recognition of relevant changes, timely care coordination, and preservation of function and autonomy.
interventions.scope: Psychiatric assessment and medication decisions remain with qualified medical clinicians.

interventions.title: Context and routine protection consultation
interventions.try: The therapist helps examine shift work, caregiving schedules, sensory demands and social pressures that complicate stability, and collaborates with the person and care team on sustainable accommodations.
interventions.measure: Track sustainable participation, manageable sleep-related demands and whether supports are available without sacrificing meaningful roles.

interventions.title: Relational uncertainty and boundary work
interventions.try: In session, the therapist differentiates valid requests for information and safety from unproductive certainty seeking, and rehearses boundaries or direct communication when appropriate.
interventions.measure: Review capacity for shared decisions, relational confidence and reduced interference from repetitive worry.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided attention flexibility practice
interventions.try: The clinician teaches and adapts a chosen attention-shifting or present-moment skill, checks for adverse effects and practices using it when worry pulls attention away from a valued task.
interventions.measure: Notice whether the person can return to chosen activities without requiring thoughts or feelings to disappear.

interventions.title: Contextual panic-access planning
interventions.try: The therapist maps where panic appears alongside actual environmental, disability or medical access barriers and helps develop safe, feasible ways to keep chosen roles available.
interventions.measure: Review participation, perceived choice and adequacy of safety or accommodation supports.
interventions.scope: Medical warning signs require appropriate assessment; do not assume every bodily symptom is panic.

interventions.title: Collaborative support-person rehearsal
interventions.try: The therapist and person identify how supporters can respond to an episode, including what helps, what feels intrusive and when medical help is indicated. They rehearse a consent-based response.
interventions.measure: Notice whether the person feels understood, safer and more able to choose next steps rather than only whether distress subsides.

interventions.title: Social demand and communication access assessment
interventions.try: In session, distinguish fear of judgment from discrimination, sensory barriers, language or communication demands. Plan reasonable changes before assigning social participation homework.
interventions.measure: Notice whether authentic participation becomes easier without requiring masking or tolerating unsafe situations.

interventions.title: Guided interpersonal experiment
interventions.try: The clinician collaborates on a voluntary, realistic interaction experiment, prepares for actual social consequences and debriefs learning rather than treating every negative outcome as a distorted belief.
interventions.measure: Review personally meaningful participation, prediction accuracy and whether communication choices are honored.

interventions.title: Therapist-led threat appraisal and risk differentiation
interventions.try: A trained therapist explores the feared outcome, actual hazards, learning history and person-defined reasons to approach or decline. They develop a working formulation before selecting exposure.
interventions.measure: Notice a clearer distinction between realistic danger and fear-based predictions and increased voluntary choice.

interventions.title: Supported approach and context coordination
interventions.try: The therapist helps arrange accessible, consensual supports for a valued situation and negotiates the role of companions so help does not become coercive or a test of compliance.
interventions.measure: Observe chosen engagement, useful supports and the person's sense of safety and control.
interventions.scope: Exclude genuinely hazardous exposures and coordinate relevant medical care.

interventions.title: OCD-specific uncertainty formulation
interventions.try: An OCD-qualified clinician maps obsessions, feared responsibility, mental rituals and neutralizing actions while distinguishing them from culturally meaningful practices or genuine safety behaviors.
interventions.measure: Review reductions in ritual-related interference and increased capacity to act with uncertainty.
interventions.scope: Avoid assigning exposure targets without consent or misclassifying medical care as ritual.

interventions.title: Values-based response prevention planning
interventions.try: In session, an appropriately trained clinician connects treatment choices to person-defined roles, clarifies what matters more than ritual rules, and collaboratively adapts ERP to consent and disability needs.
interventions.measure: Notice broader choice, engagement in valued routines and reduced OCD-driven restriction.

interventions.title: Appearance checking and avoidance intervention
interventions.try: A trained clinician collaboratively maps mirror or photo checking, camouflage, comparison and social withdrawal; when appropriate, conducts consented behavioral work tailored to the maintaining pattern.
interventions.measure: Review checking interference, freedom to participate and distress tolerance, not body appearance or attractiveness.

interventions.title: Body-image social context consultation
interventions.try: The therapist explores stigma, bullying, appearance-related discrimination and the responses of others, and helps plan protective boundaries or changes in the social environment.
interventions.measure: Measure felt dignity, safety, social participation and access to relationships without reassurance about appearance.

interventions.title: Trauma-informed relational safety work
interventions.try: A clinician and person map the effects of trust, boundaries and current relationships on recovery, establish transparent choices and practice consent-respecting support requests.
interventions.measure: Notice increased sense of agency, real-world support availability and reduction in unsafe or coercive situations.
interventions.scope: A safety plan must address current danger independently of symptom-focused therapy.

interventions.title: Trauma-related environmental access planning
interventions.try: In session, identify trauma reminders alongside actual present threats and sensory overload, then adapt settings and expectations while preserving choice about therapeutic exposure.
interventions.measure: Review chosen participation, recovery burden and whether current safety has genuinely improved.

interventions.title: Role-transition communication treatment
interventions.try: The therapist explores the meanings of a life change and helps rehearse negotiations of responsibility, boundaries and practical support with relevant people, if safe and desired.
interventions.measure: Review role functioning, collaborative decision-making and ability to ask for or decline help.

interventions.title: Life-change demand and resource formulation
interventions.try: In session, a clinician maps new demands against available time, money, housing, care responsibilities and accessibility, and collaboratively chooses practical adaptations.
interventions.measure: Notice reduced friction, more feasible routines and greater ability to meet the person's own priorities.

interventions.title: Meaning and continuing-bonds exploration
interventions.try: The therapist makes room for both pain and chosen connections with the person who died, using culturally congruent practices and the person's preferences rather than imposed closure.
interventions.measure: Notice personally meaningful remembrance, valued identity and manageable engagement in daily roles.

interventions.title: Grief-related functioning and support consultation
interventions.try: A clinician explores how bereavement intersects with exhaustion, childcare, community expectations and everyday demands, and helps negotiate accommodations and supportive connection.
interventions.measure: Review functioning with realistic supports, isolation or companionship preferences, and burden rather than a timetable for grief.

interventions.title: Environmental cue and continuity intervention
interventions.try: In session, the clinician identifies settings associated with disconnection, overload or lost time, then collaboratively tests orienting cues, routines or task supports while monitoring adverse effects.
interventions.measure: Notice continuity of chosen activities, memory support effectiveness and post-episode functioning.

interventions.title: Coordination for function and safety
interventions.try: The therapist, with permission, coordinates with appropriate clinicians or supporters about neutral observations, medical rule-outs, communication preferences and practical continuity needs.
interventions.measure: Review whether support is experienced as safe and respectful and whether important daily roles remain accessible.
interventions.scope: Do not solicit recovered memories or force interpretations of dissociative experiences.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided alternative-perspective work
interventions.try: In session, the therapist helps examine how intense emotions, relationship history and current facts can coexist, considering alternative interpretations without invalidating actual mistreatment.
interventions.measure: Observe more usable choices during interpersonal strain and personally meaningful relationship functioning.

interventions.title: Values and crisis-prevention collaboration
interventions.try: The therapist helps the person select goals that matter beyond crisis reduction, collaboratively planning safe choices and treatment continuity for periods of high arousal or changing motivation.
interventions.measure: Notice agency, continuity of support and participation in self-selected roles.
interventions.scope: Current suicide or self-harm risk still requires appropriate individualized assessment.

interventions.title: Collaborative therapy-relationship review
interventions.try: A clinician invites feedback about misunderstandings, ruptures and recurring expectations in the therapeutic relationship, using the process to refine boundaries and strengthen shared work.
interventions.measure: Review whether the person can disagree openly, experiences repair and sustains chosen relationships.

interventions.title: Interpersonal response rehearsal
interventions.try: In session, the therapist explores the consequences and context of a recurring interaction, then rehearses specific boundary-setting, listening or repair alternatives selected by the person.
interventions.measure: Notice safer communication, appropriate boundaries and valued relationship participation.

interventions.title: Stress and sensory-access support formulation
interventions.try: The therapist collaboratively identifies environmental demands, sleep disruptions, isolation or practical barriers that may intensify distress, and negotiates tolerable adjustments with the care team.
interventions.measure: Review distress, role participation and recovery costs with accommodations in place.
interventions.scope: Never delay assessment of acute medical, psychotic or safety deterioration.

interventions.title: Recovery-oriented goal negotiation
interventions.try: In session, the clinician helps the person identify roles, identity, relationships and self-defined recovery aims that are not contingent on elimination of all unusual experiences.
interventions.measure: Track personally meaningful engagement, choice, functioning and how easily support can be accessed.

interventions.title: In-session sustainable routine design
interventions.try: The clinician and person examine energy, variability, transitions and sleep or sensory demands, then build adaptable routines with recovery options instead of rigid compliance rules.
interventions.measure: Review initiation, feasible continuation, recovery effort and satisfaction with chosen supports.

interventions.title: Workplace or school support rehearsal
interventions.try: In session, the therapist helps the person prepare an accessible support request and rehearses disclosure options, boundaries and follow-up suited to their context.
interventions.measure: Notice whether requested accommodations are available and whether chosen role participation improves.

interventions.title: Neurodiversity-affirming formulation review
interventions.try: The therapist collaboratively examines distress, stigma, sensory experience and social mismatch without assuming autistic traits need correction, then revises goals around wellbeing and access.
interventions.measure: Review autonomy, distress related to barriers and ability to participate without unwanted masking.

interventions.title: Shutdown and overload recovery planning
interventions.try: In session, identify personal overload patterns and plan an individualized communication, pause and recovery approach with the person, testing whether the plan feels safe and usable.
interventions.measure: Notice lower recovery burden, respected need for breaks and preserved participation.

interventions.title: Accessible strengths-based formulation
interventions.try: The clinician uses plain language, visuals or communication aids to explore the person's preferences and understanding, checking comprehension without treating speech limits as global incapacity.
interventions.measure: Review opportunities to understand, choose, refuse and participate with agreed supports.

interventions.title: Supported daily-routine rehearsal
interventions.try: In session, the clinician and person practice a personally chosen routine with accessible cues, adjust assistance and check whether the routine serves the person's own goals.
interventions.measure: Measure participation, satisfaction and the fit of support rather than unaided independence.

interventions.title: Context-first functional behavior consultation
interventions.try: The clinician examines demands, sensory conditions, communication access, adult responses and safety risks across settings, then collaborates on environmental and relational prevention.
interventions.measure: Review unmet needs addressed, function, safety and whether replacement communication is accessible.

interventions.title: Child-centered collaborative problem solving
interventions.try: With appropriate developmental adaptation, a therapist helps caregivers and child describe concerns, agree on realistic needs and build choices without coercion or automatic blame.
interventions.measure: Notice improved communication, respect for refusal where appropriate and fewer harmful conflicts.

interventions.title: Collaborative threat-meaning and context formulation
interventions.try: The therapist reviews an escalating episode with attention to actual injustice, threat appraisals, body cues, cultural context and available alternatives, avoiding assumptions about intent.
interventions.measure: Review harm reduction, more available choices and whether legitimate boundaries can be asserted safely.

interventions.title: Relationship repair and boundary coaching
interventions.try: In session, the clinician rehearses accountability, repair, assertive requests and disengagement from unsafe conflicts, without requiring forgiveness or mutual responsibility.
interventions.measure: Track safe communication, meaningful repair when freely chosen and reduced relational harm.

interventions.title: Harm-reduction barriers consultation
interventions.try: The therapist explores access to shelter, transport, medications, safer-use resources, stigma and treatment logistics without making abstinence a precondition for support.
interventions.measure: Review access to chosen care, reduction in preventable harm and daily functioning.
interventions.scope: Immediate overdose and withdrawal risks require appropriate emergency or medical support.

interventions.title: Values-consistent change planning
interventions.try: In session, the clinician helps the person identify what they want to preserve or change about substance use and collaboratively selects a feasible next step without imposing one outcome.
interventions.measure: Notice ownership of goals, trust in treatment and person-reported benefits or harms.

interventions.title: Eating-disorder care-access problem solving
interventions.try: Within multidisciplinary treatment, the clinician explores barriers to attending specialist care, nutritional support and daily roles and coordinates needed accommodations with permission.
interventions.measure: Review medical-care access, engagement and meaningful functioning, with health indicators interpreted by qualified team members.
interventions.scope: Does not substitute for medical stabilization or prescribed nutrition plans.

interventions.title: Identity and recovery values exploration
interventions.try: A specialist therapist helps distinguish disorder-driven restrictions, personal identity and cultural values, supporting choices that align with recovery and safety in coordinated care.
interventions.measure: Review valued role engagement, sense of identity and team-monitored clinical safety.
interventions.scope: Avoid unmonitored experiments with intake, weight or exercise.

interventions.title: Shame-reducing therapeutic alliance work
interventions.try: In session, a clinician explores shame, secrecy and barriers to asking for medical and psychological help, using nonpunitive collaboration and appropriate team communication.
interventions.measure: Notice ability to seek indicated care, honesty without punishment and recovery-relevant functioning.
interventions.scope: Assessment and management of medical complications belong to the clinical team.

interventions.title: Meal-support access consultation
interventions.try: The therapist, within an appropriate treatment team, assesses practical barriers, schedules and environment that affect use of an indicated nutrition and mental-health plan.
interventions.measure: Review access to prescribed care, dignity, functioning and the person's experience of support.
interventions.scope: Do not offer generic restriction, purging or food-exposure instructions.

interventions.title: Caregiver coaching for feeding access
interventions.try: A qualified clinician and caregivers explore pressure, sensory needs and the person's communication, practicing supportive noncoercive interactions compatible with medical care.
interventions.measure: Review availability of safe intake supports, child choice and family burden.
interventions.scope: Feeding/swallowing and nutritional safety require appropriate medical or specialist oversight.

interventions.title: Predictability and sensory support planning
interventions.try: In session, the clinician and person develop routines and environmental choices that reduce eating-related overwhelm, carefully evaluating what is medically safe and personally tolerable.
interventions.measure: Notice access to eating opportunities, distress burden and clinical safety as monitored by the team.
interventions.scope: Do not use unsupported appetite or intake targets.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided sleep threat and performance work
interventions.try: The clinician explores catastrophic sleep predictions and conditioned arousal, then selects appropriate cognitive or behavioral components within a qualified sleep assessment.
interventions.measure: Review worry about sleep, daytime function, fatigue and unwanted effects.
interventions.scope: Screen for bipolar activation and relevant medical or neurological risk before restrictive sleep methods.

interventions.title: Family and caregiving sleep-demand coordination
interventions.try: In session, a therapist examines the realities of shift work, parenting, household noise and care duties and helps negotiate achievable boundaries or supports.
interventions.measure: Track next-day functioning, burden of sleep demands and whether family support is realistically available.

interventions.title: Values-led symptom-aware participation therapy
interventions.try: The clinician and person plan manageable, medically appropriate participation around persistent symptoms, modifying pace and accessibility without dismissing physical suffering.
interventions.measure: Review chosen activity, symptom interference, medical follow-through and recovery burden.
interventions.scope: Do not replace or delay evaluation of new, worsening or concerning symptoms.

interventions.title: Care-continuity and accommodation review
interventions.try: The therapist helps map fragmented appointments, communication barriers and practical demands that complicate health care, then coordinates with consent and clarifies realistic options.
interventions.measure: Notice whether essential care is easier to access and functioning is supported.

interventions.title: Therapist-guided flare-response options
interventions.try: The therapist and person explore early overload or flare cues, medically appropriate pacing and alternatives to all-or-nothing activity, rehearsing flexible responses in session.
interventions.measure: Review sustainable participation, recovery effort, valued action and symptom interference.

interventions.title: Family understanding and help negotiation
interventions.try: In session, a clinician supports communication about invisible pain, practical needs, expectations and boundaries, involving others only when wanted and safe.
interventions.measure: Notice helpful support availability, reduced conflict and the person's autonomy.

interventions.title: Person-centered cue and memory support therapy
interventions.try: A clinician observes memory and sequence demands during a chosen task and collaboratively teaches accessible external cues or habits with appropriate supporters.
interventions.measure: Review success with supports, safety, preserved choice and caregiver burden.

interventions.title: Life-role and preference continuity intervention
interventions.try: The therapist facilitates discussion of valued roles and supported decisions with the person and trusted supporters, adapting communication and obligations to actual abilities.
interventions.measure: Notice meaningful engagement, preference expression and whether decisions are respected.
interventions.scope: Decision-making ability is task-specific; reassess safety and consent as indicated.
